evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: So we talked to a lot of people everyday and most of them have one or two concerns either the movers are not showing up on time or damage to their items. Are there any of those concerns for you?
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'I would like my items not to be damaged. Ideally, but I don't have anything like super delicate or you know crazy but.' Rep reflects back with 'Okay, so what I'm hearing is that of course you don't want it to have your items to be damaged, right?' but does not dig deeper with follow-up questions or silence.
evidence_quotes.value_days: No value days discussion. October 29th was never evaluated against calendar pricing tiers, and no cheaper alternative day or date flexibility was offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep says 'We can be able to book your slot. As early as 8:30 AM to 9:00 AM we in there's no deposit required, no recent, securing your spot and if ever there will be changes then all you have to do is just simply give us a call at anytime. Would you like me to lock that in for you.' The rate lock and no deposit are mentioned, but then the customer declines ('No, I'm definitely gonna have to price compare') and the rep does not re-ask for the business. The ask is present but undermined by the customer objection and lack of overcoming it.

top_strength: Zhang gathered comprehensive logistics details across four complex stops (old storage, current apartment, new apartment, new storage) with full floor numbers, elevator access, and walking distances, then delivered a detailed itemized estimate ($3,120 for 6.5–7.5 hours with 4 movers and 2 trucks) anchored to the customer's specific scenario.
coaching_note: Step 2: after the customer raised damage as a concern, dig two layers deep with follow-up questions and silence instead of summarizing and moving on; Step 5: introduce Value Days by asking about date flexibility and offering a total dollar saving if a cheaper day exists; Step 6: always ask a genuine final concerns check ('What's still concerning you?') before attempting to close, never skip it; Step 7: when the customer declines the ask, stay in the conversation and try to overcome the objection rather than immediately pivoting to email.
